caption: Research design and as-run analysis pipeline. Certified panels from a separate data workstream feed the 2x2x2x2 model factorial, three portfolio books and a lot-level backtest under a zero-tax control and a statutory regime; committed snapshots are the only inputs to the tables and figures. Schematic: no data are plotted. The unrun and unknown items in the lower right are part of the design record.
review_note: Answers: what was run and what was not. No values, so nothing to trace. Placement: main text as a design record; it must not be read as a result.

caption: Share of in-universe security-months with certified cost inputs, by month, 2009-01 to 2019-12. Germany's investable universe is smaller than its signal-bearing one because uncertified security-months are non-tradeable and not imputed. This describes input support; it is not a performance result.
review_note: Answers: how much of the universe is tradeable on certified inputs. Definition identical across markets (certified over in-universe, per month). No uncertainty needed: a count ratio. The one-month India collapse is annotated from the data, not smoothed. Placement: main text.

caption: Capped decile composite at $1bn. (a) Gross, net and after-tax annualised Sharpe ratios by market. (b) Cost channel (net minus gross) and tax channel (after-tax minus net) in Sharpe points. Comparisons use matched books and identical definitions in all three markets. No interval is drawn because the source holds none; no net Sharpe is significantly positive. The non-executable uncapped Japanese comparator is not plotted.
review_note: Answers: where gross predictability goes under costs and tax. Same book (capped decile composite), same AUM, same definitions in all three markets. No interval is drawn because none is in the source; the figure does not claim significance. The executable and the non-executable books are not mixed. Placement: main text.

caption: B(A), the annualised mean net-return difference between capped and uncapped decile composites (Tier B), by mandate size, solvent rungs only, with unadjusted 95% bootstrap intervals. B(A) is an accounting difference against an infeasible, often near-ruined comparator; it is not realised performance, not investable, and not convertible to Sharpe points. Insolvent rungs are shaded and carry no B(A).
review_note: Answers: how the capped-minus-uncapped accounting difference grows with mandate size. Intervals are the source's unadjusted bootstrap intervals; insolvent rungs are shaded and unplotted; near-ruined comparators are hollow. Caption states B(A) is not investable performance. Placement: main text (already Figure 1 of the candidate, restyled), as an accounting illustration.

caption: Compounded terminal wealth of the uncapped comparator at solvent rungs. Where wealth is far below one the comparator is near-ruined, which is why B(A) at those rungs measures an accounting gap against an infeasible plan.
review_note: Answers: how infeasible the uncapped comparator is. Values are source terminal-wealth columns; floor-clipped points are marked. Placement: supplement.

caption: Decomposition of B(A) into gross return forgone by capping and cost saved by capping, Tier B, solvent rungs. The cost the uncapped comparator would pay dominates at large mandates.
review_note: Answers: what B(A) is made of (cost saved versus gross forgone), to prevent reading it as alpha. Placement: supplement.

intended_location: Supplement D: costs and tax by mandate size
caption: Net Sharpe and cost drag of the optimised book at $100mn, $1bn and $10bn (zero-tax regime, means over 8 prediction cells). Japan's net Sharpe is not monotone in AUM while its cost drag falls. India has one rung. Descriptive; this is not presented as confirming any prediction (amendment 001C: P2 not met, four predictions not scoreable).
review_note: Answers: how net Sharpe and cost drag move across the three AUM rungs that exist. Germany and Japan only for a line; India is a single point. Descriptive point estimates; German snapshots come from an older script version; not a confirmation of any prediction. Placement: supplement.

caption: Design-axis contrasts on the optimised book at $1bn: unadjusted t-statistics and observed size against the minimum detectable effect. The contrasts are mostly small relative to what the design could detect. Japan's conditioning contrast is exploratory and not claimed. Diagnostic only; not for the main text.
review_note: Answers: whether the design could have detected the contrasts it observed. Unadjusted t-statistics and MDE from the source; the single |t| above 1.96 is exploratory. Placement: supplement, diagnostic only; not eligible for the main text.

caption: Heatmap of the monthly share of in-universe securities with certified cost inputs, by market, 2009-01 to 2019-12. It shows where, not only how much, the required inputs are certified: Germany sits well below one throughout, India and Japan are near one apart from India's one-month collapse.
review_note: Answers: where in time certification fails. One definition for all markets; no smoothing. Placement: supplement.

caption: Decomposition of all C4 target rows into outside-the-universe, uncertified, certified-but-unusable and fully usable rows, by market. This is the denominator view behind the coverage ratio.
review_note: Answers: what the coverage denominator contains. Row-level flags, within-market shares; no performance implied. Placement: supplement.

intended_location: Supplement A: data and coverage (supports the Section 3 India disclosure)
caption: Audit of India's input coverage: monthly counts and three aggregations of the same data. One month, 2009-10, has 1 of 274 in-universe securities certified. The headline mean of 0.989 includes that month; the figure shows what the other aggregations give. It describes the flags, not any performance consequence.
review_note: Answers: whether the 0.989 headline is sensitive to one month and how it was aggregated. Uses only source counts. States what the flags cannot establish. Placement: supplement; the finding should also be disclosed in the text.

caption: Compounded wealth of the executable capped decile composite at three mandate sizes common to all markets.
review_note: Answers: how the executable book's wealth evolves at common mandate sizes. A deterministic compounding of the tracked monthly series; reproduces the published uncapped terminal wealth in tests for the uncapped counterpart. Placement: supplement.

caption: Wealth path of the capped book against the infeasible uncapped comparator at one mandate size, making the comparator's ruin visible over time.
review_note: Answers: when the infeasible comparator is ruined. Same series, same rung. Placement: supplement.

caption: Drawdowns of the capped composite at the same three mandate sizes.
review_note: Answers: depth of losses of the executable book. No inference. Placement: supplement.

caption: Monthly cost charged to the capped and uncapped books at one mandate size, showing when costs are incurred.
review_note: Answers: timing and size of the cost charged. Units stated. Placement: supplement.

caption: Calendar-year gross and net-of-cost returns of the capped composite at one mandate size.
review_note: Answers: whether results are concentrated in a few years. Descriptive. Placement: supplement.

caption: Trade size relative to average daily volume for the capped and uncapped books at the rungs of the cost-parity diagnostic.
review_note: Answers: whether the capped book respects the participation limit while the comparator does not. Source columns only. Placement: supplement.

caption: Mean gross exposure the capped decile book attains as mandates grow (Germany and India).
review_note: Answers: how binding the constraint is. Derived as 2 x (1 - cap_slack); Germany and India only, Japan absent from the source and not substituted. Placement: supplement.

caption: Number of the 8 cells whose uncapped comparator reaches a net return of -100% or worse, by market and mandate size.
review_note: Answers: where the comparator fails the solvency test. Counts from the ledger. Placement: supplement.

caption: Comparison of the two accountings of B(A) (wedge tool versus pipeline) on the rungs where both exist: close in relative terms at large B(A), but with absolute differences that grow with mandate size.
review_note: Answers: how far two accountings of the same quantity differ. They are not equal; the figure shows where and by how much and does not present the closeness at large B(A) as confirmation. Diagnostic only.

caption: Cost-parity diagnostic: cost under each accounting convention and the decomposition of their difference into trade-size basis, exit convention, borrow and interaction.
review_note: Answers: why two cost accountings differ. Accounting reconciliation only, explicitly not the exit-treatment sensitivity. Diagnostic only.

caption: Cell-level dispersion of gross, net and after-tax Sharpe ratios of the optimised book at $1bn, by market.
review_note: Answers: how much cells differ. Same rung and book across markets. No inference. Placement: supplement.

caption: Tax drag against turnover across prediction cells at $1bn, by market.
review_note: Answers: how tax drag relates to turnover. Endogeneity and confounding by statute are stated; diagnostic only.

caption: Tax drag and turnover of the optimised book across the mandate sizes that exist per market.
review_note: Answers: how tax drag and turnover change with mandate size where rungs exist. India single point. Placement: supplement.

caption: Net Sharpe of each prediction-loss cell against its economic-loss counterpart: the contrast behind the disclosed post hoc restriction to 8 of 16 cells.
review_note: Answers: why the economic arm is outside the headline. A documentation of a post hoc exclusion; not evidence for any claim. Diagnostic only.

caption: t-statistics of the three design-axis contrasts at every mandate size on the capped and uncapped decile books, Germany and India, with Holm-significant cells marked.
review_note: Answers: whether any design axis is detectable at any rung. Holm marks come from the source; missing adjusted values are marked, not filled. Placement: supplement.
